question: The figure the report gives at the end is the kilojoule form of 9 times the joule tally described below. A cam gives the follower displacement as 4 times the cube of the crank angle minus 6 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which that displacement changes at a crank angle of 2.0 is the release speed, in metres per second, of a slider whose mass is 47000 g. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is measured. A calibration offset of 1 J is subtracted from it, and a further offset of 12 J is subtracted after that, which gives the joule tally in question. What figure does the report give, in kJ?

A test bench takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0 and doubles it, reading the result as the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 44 kg. The trolley is released along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. A calibration offset of 13 J is subtracted from that reading. The bench launches 9 identical trolleys in a run and the corrected energies add. The whole run is then repeated 3 times in a shift. What is the shift total, in J?

The figure the crane display ends on is 19 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. A cam gives the hoist drum displacement as 5 times the cube of the elapsed time in seconds, with a coefficient of 0 on the square of the time, and the rate at which the drum's rate of travel is itself changing at 1.0 s is used as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a cage whose mass is 51 kg. The force the cable must apply to the cage to accelerate it that hard is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. Because a second identical cage hangs from the same beam, the beam reading is 2 times that force. What figure does the crane display end on, in kN?

The number the log ends with is 7 times the newton figure described below. During the first second of a cycle, a plunger advances at a rate equal to 2 times the square of the elapsed time plus 6 times the elapsed time. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, has 15 added to it, then 29 taken away, then 16 added back, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 153 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is the newton figure in question. The plunger bore is 55 mm. What number does the log end with, in N?

The value at the bottom of the sheet is the kilonewton form of 5 times the force described below. Between the 1st and the 2nd second of a stroke, a ram advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 6 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is multiplied by 4 and then reduced by 17, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 167000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is the force in question. What value is at the bottom of the sheet, in kN?

A depot holds 396 sleepers and 194 rail chairs, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is multiplied by 12 and then doubled, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a test wagon whose mass is 41000 g. The wagon runs on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. The depot runs 3 identical wagons and their energies add. What is the combined energy, in kJ?

A yard holds 129 clamps and 375 pins, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a trolley whose mass is 42000 g. The force the drive must apply to the trolley to accelerate it at that rate is calculated. Because 5 identical trolleys run from one drawbar the drawbar force is 5 times that, and a slack allowance of 3 N is then subtracted. The whole drawbar assembly is repeated on 4 tracks and the loads add. What is the total load, in N?

A cam on a press gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the crank angle minus 4 times the square of the crank angle. The rate at which that displacement is changing at a crank angle of 1.0 is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a tool slide whose mass is 24000 g. The force needed to accelerate the slide at that rate is calculated, and because 3 identical slides run from one frame the frame force is 3 times that, expressed in kilonewtons. A static preload of 11 kN is then added, and the whole frame is repeated across 3 bays with the loads adding. The press is driven at 150 rpm. What is the total load, in kN?

The figure the report ends on is 4 times a value that is itself 8 times a reading 20 kJ below the kilojoule figure described here. Between the 1st and the 3rd second of a stroke, a shuttle travels at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total travel over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a slug whose mass is 47000 g. The energy the slug carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that figure. What figure does the report end on, in kJ?

Between the 3rd and the 4th second of a run, a hydraulic ram advances at a rate equal to 4 times the square of the elapsed time plus 8 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 167 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide is calculated and 16 N of seal friction is subtracted from it. The remainder is expressed in kilonewtons and a release mechanism then takes a further 4 kN away. The ram runs at 190 bar. What load remains, in kN?

The number the panel displays at the end is 12 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. A relay bank has 6 identical contacts and any 2 of them may be bridged; the number of different pairs available has 18 added to it, and the result is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage whose mass is 58000 g. The force the drive must apply to the carriage to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons to give that reading. The bank runs at 110 V. What number does the panel display, in kN?

The figure the test bench reports is the kilojoule form of a joule tally that is 30 J below the one described here. A cam on a machine gives the follower displacement as 1 times the cube of the crank angle plus 5 times the square of the crank angle. The rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a crank angle of 4.0, has 13 subtracted from it, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 33 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 4 identical sliders are launched per cycle the cycle tally is 4 times that energy. What figure does the test bench report, in kJ?

The number the report ends on is 5 kJ more than the kilojoule form of the joule tally described below. Between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, a machine slide advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 4 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test block whose mass is 47 kg. The energy the block carries because of its motion is recorded and a calibration offset of 25 J is subtracted from it. The machine runs 12 identical blocks in a batch and the corrected energies add to give the tally in question. What number does the report end on, in kJ?

The number the log ends with is 24 kJ more than 4 times a figure that is itself 10 times the kilojoule reading described below. A trolley of mass 23000 g is released along a level bench, and its release speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 21 = 0. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The bench is 3.5 m long. What number does the log end with, in kJ?

A cam gives the follower displacement as 5 times the cube of the crank angle plus 2 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which that displacement is changing at a crank angle of 1.0 is the release speed, in metres per second, of a slider whose mass is 49000 g. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. The machine launches 11 identical sliders per cycle and their energies add. A trigger circuit then adds 24 kJ to the cycle total and a damper absorbs 21 kJ of it. The crank turns at 75 rpm. What energy remains in the cycle total, in kJ?

The number the log ends with is 7 times the newton figure described below. Between the 2nd and the 4th second of a run, a linear drive advances at a rate equal to 2 times the square of the elapsed time plus 3 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage whose mass is 100 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated, then 29 N of bearing drag is subtracted, then a preload of 17 N is added, and finally a further 27 N of clamp force is added, giving the newton figure in question. The rail is 12 m long. What number does the log end with, in N?

The number the day sheet ends with is 23 J more than a value that is 10 J below a value that is itself 5 J above the joule tally described here. A test bench takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0 and reads it as the release speed in metres per second of a trolley whose mass is 29000 g. The trolley runs along a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. The bench launches 12 identical trolleys in a run and their energies add to give that tally. What number does the day sheet end with, in J?

The figure the report ends on is 3 kJ less than 3 times a value that is itself 12 times the kilojoule reading described below. Between the 1st and the 4th second of a stroke, a ram advances at a rate equal to 3 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a slug whose mass is 7000 g. The energy the slug carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The ram runs at 160 bar. What figure does the report end on, in kJ?

A workshop holds 223 spindles and 116 chucks, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley whose mass is 47000 g on a level bench. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded, and a calibration offset of 17 J is subtracted from it. The bench runs 10 identical trolleys per round and 6 rounds per shift, and all the corrected energies add. What is the shift total, in kJ?

The figure the rig totals at the end is 7 times a value that is 29 kN more than the kilonewton reading described below. A cam on a press gives the follower displacement as 3 times the cube of the crank angle minus 4 times the square of the crank angle, and the rate at which that displacement changes at a crank angle of 1.0 is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of a slide whose mass is 194 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated, and a tare of 10 N from the load cell is added to it. That total, expressed in kilonewtons, is the reading in question. What figure does the rig total, in kN?

The number the bench prints last is 8 J less than 6 times a figure that is itself 10 J below a value 4 J under the energy described here. A launcher takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0 and reads it as the release speed, in metres per second, of a puck whose mass is 40 kg on a level air table. The energy the puck carries because of its motion at that speed is the energy in question. What number does the bench print last, in J?

A conveyor controller takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0 and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A crate of mass 109000 g is accelerated at that rate by the belt, and the force the belt must apply to the crate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. A drum tension of 23 kN is added to it, and a take-up weight adds a further 13 kN. Because 12 identical belts run in the hall, the load the hall frame carries is 12 times that figure. The belt runs at 45 rpm. What is that load, in kN?

The figure the commissioning sheet ends on is 8 kN less than the kilonewton reading described below. A press controller adds its two calibration constants 8 and 2 and multiplies the sum by 3, treating the result as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A tool head of mass 146 kg is accelerated at that rate and the force the drive must apply to it is calculated. Because 6 heads run per frame and 5 frames stand in the hall, the hall load is that force multiplied by 6 and then by 5, expressed in kilonewtons, which is the reading in question. The press stands 4.2 m tall. What figure does the commissioning sheet end on, in kN?

A patch bay has 8 identical ports and any 2 of them may be linked; the number of different links available is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test mass of 53000 g on the rail beside it. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 12 identical masses are launched per run the run energy is 12 times that value. A trigger coil then adds 15 J to the run energy and a lamp circuit adds a further 11 J. The bay is rated at 48 V. What does the run energy come to, in kJ?

The number the log ends with is 22 N more than a figure that is 28 N below 12 times the force described here. Between the 1st and the 2nd second of a stroke, a ram advances at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 5 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that interval, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 191000 g. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is the force in question. The ram runs at 175 bar. What number does the log end with, in N?
